title: Lemon and eucalyptus outdoor soy candle
subtitle: A container soy candle for outdoor tables and terraces
excerpt: A soy container candle scented with lemon and eucalyptus essential oils, intended for outdoor use on terraces and in garden spaces. The citrus-fresh scent helps mask the sweet smells that attract insects. Makes one 200 ml jar candle.
sourceNotes: Soy wax container candle formulation: general candlemaking reference. Lemon and eucalyptus essential oils as insect-deterrent fragrance: open-access reference on plant-based insect deterrents. Essential oil toxic to cats and dogs: ASPCA database (aspca.org). Candle fire safety: British Standard BS EN 15494:2019 (candle warning label requirements).

recipe.yieldDescription: 1 jar candle (~150 g soy wax fill, 200 ml jar)
recipe.batchNotes: Pour four or five jars in one session; one batch of melted wax goes further than a single jar.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cure for at least one week before the first burn. The wax needs time to fully bond with the jar.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keeps two years unlit in a cool, dark place. The citrus essential oils fade fastest; the candle will still burn cleanly but the scent throw will diminish after 12 months. Discard if the wax surface shows significant cracking or the wick has come loose from the base.

glossaryTerms.definition: The temperature at which melted wax is poured into the jar. For container soy wax, the standard pour temperature is 55 to 65°C. Too hot and the wax shrinks away from the jar walls as it cools, leaving gaps. Too cool and the wax sets before it has levelled.

content.text: A soy container candle for outdoor tables, windowsills, and terraces. Lemon and eucalyptus essential oils give a sharp, clean citrus-and-herb scent that works well in open air where heavy fragrance dissipates quickly. The
for container soy wax is 55 to 65°C; pour at the cooler end in warm weather.
Lemon and eucalyptus essential oils are toxic to cats and dogs. Never leave a burning candle unattended, near flammable materials, or within reach of children.

items.prepNote: container-grade soy wax; roughly 140 g fills a 200 ml jar to the standard fill line
3% of wax weight; adds a fresh herbal depth
pre-tabbed cotton wick sized for a 200 ml jar (typically CD-12 or ECO-6 for soy wax in a 6 cm diameter jar)

content.text: Warm the jar gently in a low oven (50°C) for five minutes to prevent thermal shock when the wax is poured. Stick the wick tab to the centre of the jar base with a drop of hot glue or wick sticker. Rest the wick across the centring bar laid across the jar mouth so the wick stands upright and centred.
Weigh the soy wax into the pouring pitcher. Melt over a bain-marie on low heat, stirring occasionally. Remove from the heat when fully liquid. Let cool to 60°C, checking with the probe thermometer.
At 60°C, add both essential oils and stir thoroughly for one minute. Pour steadily into the warmed jar in one smooth motion. Pour to roughly 1 cm below the jar rim.
Leave to cool at room temperature overnight. Do not move the jar while it is setting. Once solid, trim the wick to 5 mm above the wax surface. Leave to cure for one week before lighting.

On the first burn, allow the wax to melt all the way to the edge of the jar before extinguishing. For a 200 ml jar this typically takes two to three hours. This sets the wax memory and prevents tunnelling on subsequent burns.

Store unlit candles in a cool, dark place. Two years shelf life. The citrus essential oils fade faster than woody or resinous fragrance oils; the scent throw diminishes after 12 months but the candle still burns safely.
